_meta.description: Document-rules config for written_statement — Defendant's written statement under Order VIII CPC with counter-claim and set-off provisions
_meta.change_protocol: All edits require CLO sign-off. Para-wise denial structure and 30/120-day limitation are non-negotiable.

title: Written Statement (Order VIII CPC)

causeTitle.caseNomenclature: Civil Suit No. _____ of [YEAR] / Commercial Suit No. _____ of [YEAR]

fields.label: Date of service of summons on defendant
Days from service of summons (must be within 30; extendable to 120 in non-commercial, max 120 in commercial)
If beyond 30 days, application for condonation with sufficient cause
Preliminary objections (Order VIII R.2) — maintainability, limitation, jurisdiction, mis-joinder, non-joinder, cause of action absent
Para-wise admit / deny structure — list each paragraph of plaint and response
Specific admissions (Order VIII R.5 — failure to deny = deemed admission)
Additional pleas / facts not pleaded by plaintiff but defendant relies on (Order VIII R.2)
Set-off claimed under Order VIII R.6 (ascertained money debt mutually due)
Counter-claim — cause of action, relief, valuation, court fee on counter-claim
Documents relied upon by defendant (Order VIII R.1A)
Prayer — dismissal + costs + counter-claim relief if any

mandatory_clauses.name: Preliminary Objections — Order VIII R.2
mandatory_clauses.description: Maintainability / jurisdiction / limitation / cause of action / mis-joinder / non-joinder

mandatory_clauses.name: Para-wise Admission / Denial — Order VIII R.3-5
mandatory_clauses.description: Specific denial of each material allegation. Evasive denial is no denial (R.4). Failure to deny = deemed admission (R.5).

mandatory_clauses.name: Additional Facts — Order VIII R.2
mandatory_clauses.description: Any matter showing suit not maintainable / illegality / fraud / Limitation Act bar / payment / release / discharge — must be specifically pleaded

mandatory_clauses.name: Set-off — Order VIII R.6 (if claimed)
mandatory_clauses.description: Ascertained sum of money legally recoverable; both parties fill same character; suit valuation enough; court fee on set-off

mandatory_clauses.name: Counter-claim — Order VIII R.6A-6G (if pleaded)
mandatory_clauses.description: Treated as cross-suit; cause of action must accrue before filing WS; court fee payable; valuation must be within court's pecuniary jurisdiction

mandatory_clauses.name: Denial / Acknowledgement of Plaintiff's Documents
mandatory_clauses.description: Order VIII R.1A — defendant to disclose documents relied upon and respond to plaintiff's list

mandatory_clauses.name: Prayer
mandatory_clauses.description: Dismissal of suit + costs + relief on counter-claim (if any)

mandatory_clauses.name: Affidavit in support — Order VI R.15(4)
Statement of Truth — Order VI R.15A (Commercial Courts only)

verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {defendant_name}, son/daughter/wife of {defendant_father_name}, aged about {defendant_age} years, resident of {defendant_address}, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs ___ to ___ of the above Written Statement are true to my personal knowledge, paragraphs ___ to ___ are based on records maintained by me, and paragraphs ___ to ___ are matters of legal submission believed true on advice of counsel. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Defendant

promptInstructions: Draft a Written Statement strictly under Order VIII CPC.

TIME LIMIT: Order VIII R.1 — file WS within 30 days of service of summons. Court may extend to 120 days (in non-commercial suits) on recorded reasons for sufficient cause, with cost. In Commercial Courts, 120 days is the OUTER LIMIT and beyond it WS cannot be filed (SCG Contracts v. KS Chamankar 2019).
Cite: SCG Contracts (India) Pvt Ltd v. KS Chamankar Infrastructure Pvt Ltd (2019) 12 SCC 210 — 120-day limit in commercial suits is mandatory and inflexible.

PARA-WISE ADMISSION / DENIAL — the core structure of WS. Each material allegation in plaint must be: (a) specifically admitted; (b) specifically denied; or (c) denial of knowledge (only where defendant has no knowledge and cannot reasonably be expected to have).
Order VIII R.3 — Denial must be specific. General denial is no denial.
Order VIII R.4 — Evasive denial is no denial. If defendant disputes a fact, he must answer the substance.
Order VIII R.5 — Specific denial. Every allegation of fact in plaint, if not denied specifically or by necessary implication, shall be taken as admitted (DEEMED ADMISSION).
Para 1: Cause title with suit reference.
Para 2-onwards: PRELIMINARY OBJECTIONS first — maintainability, jurisdiction, limitation, mis-joinder/non-joinder, no cause of action, bar of res judicata, bar under any statute.
Then: PARA-WISE RESPONSE — 'In response to paragraph 1 of the plaint, the Defendant denies / admits / states...' for each paragraph.

After para-wise response: ADDITIONAL PLEAS (Order VIII R.2) — affirmative defences. Must specifically plead: limitation, payment, release, discharge, illegality, fraud, misrepresentation, want of consideration, lack of authority etc. (failure to specifically plead = waiver).
Cite: Badat & Co v. East India Trading Co AIR 1964 SC 538 — specific pleas mandatory.

SET-OFF (Order VIII R.6) — defendant may, where suit is for recovery of money, claim set-off against plaintiff's claim. Conditions: (i) suit for ascertained sum; (ii) set-off claim also for ascertained sum legally recoverable; (iii) within court's pecuniary jurisdiction; (iv) both parties fill same character. Court fee payable on set-off as if separate plaint.
EQUITABLE SET-OFF — judicial creation, allowed where claims arise out of same transaction (not just ascertained sums).

COUNTER-CLAIM (Order VIII R.6A-6G) — defendant may set up cross-claim. Conditions: (i) cause of action accrued before filing WS; (ii) within pecuniary jurisdiction of court; (iii) court fee payable. Counter-claim treated as cross-suit; plaintiff files written statement in reply to counter-claim. Final decree disposes both.
Cite: Ashok Kumar Kalra v. Wing Cdr Surendra Agnihotri (2020) — counter-claim must be filed before issues are framed; outer limit similar to WS time.
Order VIII R.1A — defendant to produce documents relied upon along with WS.
Order VIII R.9 — no pleading subsequent to WS other than by way of defence to set-off / counter-claim, except with leave of court.
PRAYER — dismissal of suit with costs + relief on counter-claim/set-off.
Verification — Order VI R.15 — categorise paragraphs by source (knowledge / records / legal advice).
Affidavit in support — Order VI R.15(4) — mandatory.
Statement of Truth — Order VI R.15A — mandatory in Commercial Courts (post 2018 amendments to CPC and CCA Schedule).
Tone: precise, point-by-point. Avoid argumentative language. Avoid evasive denials.
Append Lawie disclaimer.

sections.description: Written statement — 30 days, extendable; 120 days outer limit in commercial
Duty of defendant to produce documents
New facts must be specially pleaded
Procedure when party fails to present WS
Order VIII R.1 proviso — 120 days outer limit for WS in commercial suits
Amendments to CPC for commercial disputes
Bar of limitation — court must dismiss suit if barred even if no plea taken (but defendant must still plead)

filing_checklist: Written Statement (original + copies for plaintiff and court)
Affidavit in support of WS (Order VI R.15(4))
Statement of Truth (if Commercial Court — Order VI R.15A)
Court fee on counter-claim (if any) — ad valorem as separate plaint
List of documents (Order VIII R.1A) with index
Application for extension of time (if filed beyond 30 days) with reasons and cost offered
Application for leave to file counter-claim (post-Ashok Kumar Kalra timeline)
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: days_from_service must not exceed 30 unless delay_application provided
In commercial suits, days_from_service cannot exceed 120 (SCG Contracts)
para_wise_denial must not be empty — each material para of plaint addressed
additional_pleas must not be empty (limitation / payment / fraud etc. specifically pleaded if relied upon)
If counter_claim=true, counter_claim_court_fee must be > 0 and counter_claim_amount must be within court pecuniary jurisdiction
If set_off=true, set_off_amount must be ascertained and within court jurisdiction
advocate_enrollment must match Bar Council format
key_citations: SCG Contracts (India) Pvt Ltd v. KS Chamankar Infrastructure Pvt Ltd (2019) 12 SCC 210 — 120-day outer limit for WS in commercial suits is mandatory
Salem Advocate Bar Association (II) v. Union of India (2005) 6 SCC 344 — 90-day extension is procedural and not absolute bar in non-commercial
Kailash v. Nankhu (2005) 4 SCC 480 — Time for filing WS in non-commercial — directory not mandatory; sufficient cause needed beyond 90
Ashok Kumar Kalra v. Wing Cdr Surendra Agnihotri (2020) 2 SCC 394 — Counter-claim timing — outer limit before framing of issues
Badat & Co v. East India Trading Co AIR 1964 SC 538 — Specific pleadings; vague denials insufficient
Lohia Properties (P) Ltd v. Atmaram Kumar (1993) 4 SCC 6 — Order VIII R.5 deemed admission rule
Ramesh Chand Ardawatiya v. Anil Panjwani (2003) 7 SCC 350 — Counter-claim is independent cross-suit
